correctness.summary: The exact signed flat-chaos cumulant generating function yields the cubic and quartic Cramer corrections; saddlepoint tilting matches the normal Mills prefactor on the stated range; independence then transfers the relative-tail correction to translated Gumbel maxima and an explicit Kolmogorov limit. Positive and balanced specializations, together with the m asymptotic to (log p)^(5/2) witness, give the same-effective-rank separation.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical Cramer-Petrov theory, Fang-Koike's flat centered-chi-square Wiener-chaos example, and high-dimensional zero-skewness CLT results already explain the generic log^3 and log^2 scales, so those exponents are not claimed as new. Searches found no prior statement of the sign-imbalance extreme-tail expansion, the exact critical Gumbel translations and Kolmogorov constants, or the explicit same-r4/same-fourth-cumulant separation for flat signed Gaussian quadratic-chaos maxima. Older triangular-array extreme-value literature remains the main residual risk.

value.summary: The result supplies sharp independent flat-spectrum benchmarks for a new effective-rank phase-transition theory and proves that effective rank alone cannot be a sharp universal phase coordinate: spectral sign imbalance and the third cumulant change the dimensional Gaussianization threshold by a full logarithmic power.

limitations: The p chaos coordinates are independent.
All nonzero eigenvalues have equal magnitude.
The Cramer expansion is stated when m/(log p)^(5/3) tends to infinity.
The result concerns the Gaussian-chaos target, not the separate finite-sample U-statistic-to-chaos approximation.
Generic log^3 and zero-skew log^2 moderate-deviation phenomena are prior art.
Older triangular-array extreme-value literature was not exhaustively inspected.
Independent audit has not been performed.
review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
